disputes.reason: Decompile shows this is pure Bink movie-playback glue: it calls the Bink import thunks directly (_BinkSetSoundSystem@8, _BinkOpen@8, _BinkPause@8, _BinkNextFrame@4, _BinkWait@4, _BinkDoFrame@4, _BinkCopyToBuffer@28, _BinkClose@4) inside a PeekMessage/TranslateMessage/DispatchMessage pump that checks for ESC/Space to skip the movie. There is nothing main.c-generic about it; per the module-fencing rule Bink-related code should be labelled lib:bink (or at minimum 'cutscene' for the movie-skip logic), not 'main'. The assigning agent's own evidence string ('lone object file... called from game startup functions') already flags this as an isolated object file rather than an actual main.c function, and gave it only 0.4 confidence.

Function returns the literal strings "couldn't open file" / "couldn't write header" / "couldn't write row" while writing a header then looping rows via FUN_00555a90/FUN_00555890 (open/write/close-style calls outside this slice). The slice's own cea-pdb hint explicitly names the CE-source match: 'targa_export (main)' for this exact string set. This is a debug TGA-dump utility, not part of the bitmap tag-processing code that surrounds it (contrast with 0x43f030/0x43f250/0x43f290, which genuinely reference bitmap-group globals like DAT_0087bc14, or 0x43ffe0, which does real DXT endpoint interpolation). The agent appears to have swept this one function into the surrounding bitmaps run by address proximity while ignoring its own hint data naming it main's targa_export.
